# Test fixtures

## ⚠️ The top-level `*.json` files are SYNTHETIC

The environment this project was written in could not reach `www.mvg.de`,
`api.open-meteo.com` or `efa.mvv-muenchen.de` (outbound connections were
denied by the sandbox's egress policy — see DECISIONS.md). These files were
therefore generated by `tools/make_synthetic_fixtures.py` from the publicly
known response shapes of:

| File | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| `mvg_locations_freiheit.json` | `GET https://www.mvg.de/api/bgw-pt/v3/locations?query=…&locationTypes=STATION` |
| `mvg_departures_freiheit.json`, `mvg_departures_gauting.json` | `GET …/v3/departures?globalId=…&limit=…` |
| `mvg_departures_alt_shape.json` | deliberately *different* shape (wrapped object, renamed fields, seconds) to test parser tolerance |
| `mvg_messages.json` | `GET …/v3/messages` |
| `openmeteo_munich.json` | `GET https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?…&timeformat=unixtime` |

All times are relative to `FIXTURE_NOW = 1791475200` (2026-10-08 18:00 CEST).

## Real captures

Run `tools/fetch_fixtures.sh` on a machine with internet access. It writes
`test/fixtures/real/*.json`. The test `test_real_fixtures` parses them if they
exist (and is skipped otherwise), checking that the parsers find plausible
data in genuine responses. Commit them if you want CI to keep checking.
